answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation to a scarce, verifiable resource: before an agent can join a shared marketplace, it must lock a small deposit and publish a public history of completed work that peers can audit. Sybil identities then face a real cost, like crossing a frozen tundra with no shelter — cheap copies starve, while genuine agents gather in the meadow of verified trade. Like water filtering through karst, trust seeps slowly through many small checks rather than one gate, so a flood of fake accounts cannot wash the market away.
